# Garcia warns Belgium against complaceny despite 5-0 friendly win
[...]
### Belgium put on a show in front of goal against Tunisia, but even though they kept a clean sheet, Rudi Garcia wants more from his defence.
[...]
Despite a 5-0 win over 10-man Tunisia in their final pre-World Cup friendly, Rudi Garcia warned Belgium against getting complacent in defence.
[...]
The Red Devils enjoyed a dominant first half, though they only led 1-0 at the break, with Leandro Trossard getting the goal in the 28th minute.
[...]
However, after Charles De Ketelaere added
[...]

[...]
gates opened.
[...]
Kevin De Bruyne, Dodi Lukebakio and Nicolas Raskin all got on the scoresheet, and Belgium finished the match with 27 shots on goal worth 4.1 expected goals (xG), with 12 shots on target.
[...]
Garcia switched back to a four-man defence, having seen a successful trial with three at the back during their 2-0 win over Croatia, and he sees lessons to be learned from how they played against Tunisia.
[...]
"It is a wake-up call. It is sometimes good for a coach to be able to emphasise that the players must always be focused, always go to the limit," Garcia said.
[...]
"I told them that I was not satisfied and that they needed to pull themselves together.
[...]
"Between minutes 55 and 60, we lost the ball. It was just like in training. We defended with six, not eleven.
[...]
"It should be the other way around. We even almost let Tunisia get back into the match. Afterwards, we recovered.
[...]
"We won't win 5-0 every time at the World Cup. Don't forget that we also played against ten men for a long time.
[...]
"But okay, we have gained confidence, and everyone has been able to get some minutes. Morale is pretty much at maximum. And I think we can do even better."

Belgium are seeking to temper any expectations after an impressive away victory in Croatia ⁠on Tuesday, where a goal from Romelu Lukaku came as a major boost ahead of the World Cup.

Belgium’s top scorer netted his ‌90th international goal in the 2-0 win, as both countries continued World Cup preparations, ‌marking his return to the team after a 12-month absence and ‌seemingly putting behind him a difficult season in which he played less than ‌an hour’s football for Napoli.

[...]
“Our top scorer, our super top ‌scorer, has scored again, and that's fantastic. That goal is good for his ​confidence. Still, we have to remain cautious. It can be dangerous to rush things. We need to bring him along ​step by step,” the coach told reporters.
